_doc: What can be cleared on a Mac, as data. clearables.sh finds and removes by these rules; files.js draws them.
Nothing outside this file knows a rule by name: the shell knows a few finder kinds, the page knows verdict fields.
find.kind: marker (a project file beside a regenerable folder, any depth under ~), path (globs, each match one row),
children (each child of a globbed folder is one row), ext (files by extension under ~), big (one huge log-like file),
series (a folder of many dated files nothing prunes), cmd (a read-only shell snippet printing 'path<TAB>k=v;k=v').
remove.method: tool (cmd run in cwd, placeholders {project} {name} {parent}), purge (rm -rf), trash (recoverable),
report (never removed here; the row offers remove.cmd to copy). fallback applies when the tool is not installed.
safety is the base verdict; active_days demotes a SAFE row to REVIEW when it was used that recently;
min_age_days does the same for young files. The page never promotes a verdict, only demotes.
Order matters: the first rule to reach a folder claims it, so specific rules come before general ones.
subject is the why line's first part: {label} {name} {parent} and any key the finder emits ({project}, {model}, …).
age_label names the row's last-used time ("last built 71 days ago"); rules without it show no age.

walk._doc: One find over ~ serves every marker, ext, big and series rule. Pruned trees are never walked.

rules.label: Ollama model

find.sh: find "$HOME/.ollama/models/manifests" -type f 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r m; do t=${m##*/}; n=${m%/*}; n=${n##*/}; b=$(grep -oE '"size":[0-9]+' "$m" | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END {print s+0}'); printf '%s\tmodel=%s:%s;bytes=%s\n' "$m" "$n" "$t" "$b"; done

rules.regen: `ollama pull` downloads it again — many GB

rules.label: iPhone backup

find.sh: for d in "$HOME/Library/Application Support/MobileSync/Backup"/*; do [ -f "$d/Info.plist" ] || continue; n=$(plutil -extract 'Device Name' raw -o - "$d/Info.plist" 2>/dev/null | tr ';|' '  '); t=$(plutil -extract 'Last Backup Date' raw -o - "$d/Info.plist" 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\tdevice=%s;date=%s\n' "$d" "$n" "$t"; done

rules.regen: not rebuilt — make sure a newer backup exists first
